headline: Non-text AI model Jev valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch
summary: TypeSafe AI, the company behind the rapidly adopted Jev model, has raised $870 million. A third of Fortune 500 companies are reportedly using Jev, which focuses on automation rather than text generation.
details: TypeSafe AI, developer of the non-text AI model Jev, has secured $870 million in funding, valuing the company at $7.5 billion. This substantial investment round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with additional participation from Sequoia and existing investor DCVC.

The massive fundraise follows Jev's viral success almost immediately after its September 15 release. The startup claims that a remarkable one-third of Fortune 500 companies are already utilizing the model, indicating swift enterprise adoption.

Jev is built on a transformer architecture but differs from large language models (LLMs) by not outputting text. Instead, it produces probabilities, which the company refers to as "calibrated decisions."

What excites users and large corporations about Jev is TypeSafe's assertion that it operates significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than traditional LLMs. The company positions its unique approach as ideally suited for automating tasks, rather than generating text or code.

TypeSafe AI was co-founded in 2024 by Diogo Almeida, a former OpenAI researcher, Sasha Sheng, previously a Meta research engineer, and Erik Gafni, an engineer and entrepreneur. Almeida noted that while human language AI is advanced, it's less effective for automation, which computers handle differently.

headline_marked: [[Google teases Fitbit Edge]] wearable, revealing name and October 12 reveal date
headline: Google teases Fitbit Edge wearable, revealing name and October 12 reveal date
summary: Google's upcoming fitness tracker, the Fitbit Edge, is positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch 5. It's rumored to cost around $200 and offer up to 7 days of battery life.
details: Google has officially teased its new fitness tracker, confirming the name 'Fitbit Edge' and an October 12 reveal date. This follows earlier leaks and sightings in Pixel 11 marketing.

The wearable is expected to bridge the gap between the screenless Fitbit Air and the more premium Pixel Watch 5. Google's social media posts used the caption 'Get an Edge on your health. 10.12.26' to confirm the details.

Previous reports from Android Headlines and Dealabs detailed its features, battery life, and estimated price. It's rumored to offer up to seven days of battery with the always-on display disabled, or two days with it active.
The estimated price point is around €179 (approximately $200) in Europe, potentially closer to $180 in the US. This positions it as a significant step up from the $99 Fitbit Air.

The Fitbit Edge would be Google's first similarly-sized fitness tracker release since the Fitbit Charge 6 in 2023. It aims to be a natural upgrade for users and may encourage subscriptions to Google Health Premium.
